name: Type II fibre (fast-twitch)
short_description: The fast-twitch family of human skeletal muscle fibre, built to contract quickly and forcefully via anaerobic glycolysis rather than to last. The family is not one fibre but two related types, Type IIa and Type IIx, which sit at different points on the same fast design -- so this entry is rendered as a small bundle of two adjacent fibres, one styled IIa (moderate mitochondria, pale rose, richer capillary bed) and one styled IIx (sparse mitochondria, near-white cream, thin capillary), sharing the same cross-striated, peripherally-nucleated architecture but visibly differing in colour, mitochondrial density and capillary supply.

textbook.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; first attempt). Two-fibre bundle composition, both running diagonally off all four edges -- corner check TL=(56,56,58) background, TR=(242,229,225) fibre, BL=(228,177,177) fibre, BR=(57,57,59) background, i.e. correct diagonal fill, and zoomed crops of both exit corners confirmed the fibre body colour runs straight into the corner pixels with no rounded end-cap and no background triangle at either end. Striation checked by magnified ~30% crops on BOTH fibres, not just one: outer surface of each fibre shows transverse dark/pale bands with a fine slate Z-line at the centre of each pale band running the full visible length, AND fine lengthwise myofibril striping is visible within each cutaway window underneath -- both patterns present at once on both fibres. IIa (upper-left) vs IIx (lower-right) differentiation clearly visible: IIa is a darker dusty rose with 6+ larger amber-ochre mitochondria in its cutaway and a denser look; IIx is distinctly paler pink-cream, visibly wider, with sparse small dots in its cutaway. A single shared crimson capillary runs in the endomysium gap between the two fibres rather than two separately-thicknessed vessels (a compromise from the prompt's ask for 'thicker for IIa, thinner for IIx' -- recorded honestly, not smoothed over; the colour/mitochondria differentiation, which is the primary and most legible distinguishing signal, is unaffected). Used as final and as the SVG base.

sem.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; first attempt). Surface-only false-colour SEM of two ridged tubes side by side, separated by a shallow groove. Framing: corners TL=(50,55,63) background, TR=(210,193,189) fibre, BL=(233,217,214) fibre, BR=(37,41,51) background -- correct diagonal fill; magnified corner crops confirm both fibres run off all four exit points with no end-cap. Striation checked by a 30%-frame magnified crop centred on the ridge texture: fine, closely-spaced ridges encircle BOTH tubes perpendicular to the long axis (true transverse rings, the surface expression of A/I banding), continuous the whole visible length -- this is the medium-appropriate check for SEM (surface only; no interior banding claim made). Colour differentiation: upper-left tube is a distinctly deeper dusty rose (IIa), lower-right tube is paler, near-white pink-cream and visibly wider (IIx) -- clearly two different surface tones, satisfying the entry's core requirement even though SEM cannot show mitochondria or capillaries (surface-only medium; per project convention this style gets no labelled SVG, so the interior differentiators are carried by the other three styles instead). Used as final.

3d.1: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; first attempt). Two-fibre bundle, soft translucent tones. Framing: corners TL=(4,7,12) background, TR=(195,148,148) fibre, BL=(238,208,200) fibre, BR=(3,6,11) background -- correct; magnified corner crops (top-right and bottom-left) show both fibres' body colour running straight into the corner with no end-cap disc. Striation checked on BOTH fibres by magnified crops: transverse A/I banding with a fine slate Z-disc line crossing in register is clearly visible in each fibre's cutaway, together with fine lengthwise myofibril striping on the surface above/around each cutaway -- both patterns present simultaneously on both fibres, not just one. IIa (upper) vs IIx (lower) differentiation is the strongest of the three illustrated styles here: IIa's cutaway and flanking surface carry six-plus large, clearly-modelled amber-ochre mitochondria plus a substantial crimson capillary running alongside; IIx's cutaway and surface carry only small sparse tan dots and its capillary flank is noticeably thinner and less prominent -- an honest, visible thickness difference in this style (unlike textbook/watercolor's single shared vessel). Used as final and as the 3d SVG base.

watercolor.1: fail (gemini-3-pro-image; framing). Correct palette, striation and IIa/IIx colour differentiation, aged paper filling the frame edge-to-edge (all 4 corners paper-toned, confirmed by pixel sample and by scanning full edge rows/columns for a border line -- none found). FAILED on framing: both fibres show a complete, closed, rounded end-cap at the top-right exit, fully inside the canvas with a visible paper margin around the ellipse on every side -- the classic 'stubby sausage' defect the brief calls out by name, caught by zooming into the top-right and bottom-left corners specifically (not by the corner-pixel test alone, which only checks background vs. fibre colour and would have passed this attempt; the pixel test does not discriminate a capped end from a genuinely cropped one, so both checks are needed). Fix-prompt: scale the fibre bundle much larger/closer so both ends are geometrically forced off-canvas, and explicitly forbid a complete oval end-cap surrounded by paper on every side.
watercolor.2: pass (gemini-3-pro-image; scaled-up, closer-cropped composition). Re-verified corner pixels (all four paper-toned, as expected for this style's full-bleed-paper rule) AND magnified crops of the top-right and bottom-left exit points: both fibres now run straight into the corner with the wash colour touching the edge pixels directly, no closed end-cap outline anywhere, no paper margin at either tip. Striation re-checked by a magnified crop: fine ink hatching (lengthwise myofibrils) plus a perpendicular double ink line crossing it at intervals (the A-band/Z-disc divider) are both present at once -- confirmed this is a real transverse marking and not just more lengthwise hatching by inspecting the crossing angle directly, since the set's own lesson warns that lengthwise texture alone can look convincing at a glance. IIa (upper-left, darker rose wash, denser kidney-bean mitochondria) vs IIx (lower-right, paler cream wash, sparser dots, visibly wider) clearly differentiated. A single shared capillary (soft crimson wash) runs in the endomysium gap, same compromise as textbook, recorded once rather than twice. Used as final and as the watercolor SVG base.

reference: pass (2026-08-23). Bloemberg & Quadrilatero (2012) PLoS ONE 7(4):e35273, Fig 1A (cropped to panel A from the 2x2 original), CC BY 4.0. Viewed at full resolution: five to six false-coloured fibre cross-sections (blue=I, green=IIA, red=IIB, unstained black=IIX) with the original authors' own baked-in identity labels intact and legible after the crop. No scale bar; the plate's own thin panel border and a small 'A' corner tag were present in the source and are acceptable on a reference image not used as an SVG base. Upscale recorded explicitly: source panel A cropped to 632x463, centre-cropped to 463x463 square by fetch_reference.py, then upscaled to 1080x1080 (a real upscale, roughly 2.3x linear). Honest caveats recorded in the render.md and repeated here because they matter for THIS umbrella entry specifically: (1) rat tissue, not human -- the red IIB fibres shown are real rodent fibres that do not correspond to any member of the human Type II family this entry depicts; (2) the stain has no positive marker for IIx -- those fibres are identified by exclusion (unstained by all three antibodies), weaker evidence than a direct positive stain; (3) this is a cross-section, so it was NOT used to justify anything about transverse A/I banding or peripheral-nucleus position in the renders -- those checks were made against the science text and against magnified crops of the renders themselves.
decision: used as final (gemini-3-pro-image), first attempt. Two clearly-differentiated fibres (IIa darker/denser-mito, IIx paler/sparser-mito), correct diagonal framing at all 4 corners verified by pixel sample AND magnified corner crops, transverse+longitudinal striation confirmed on both fibres by magnified crops. 10-label SVG built; every anchor pixel-sampled against the raw base render and corrected where it missed (sarcolemma, a_band, z_disc and iix_fibre anchors were initially off-target -- one landed in pure background -- and were re-picked using colour-channel scans plus zoomed crops before the final SVG build). Compromise: a single shared capillary in the endomysium gap rather than two visibly different-thickness vessels; recorded, not hidden.

used as final (gemini-3-pro-image), first attempt. Best differentiation of the three illustrated styles: visibly different mitochondria density AND capillary thickness between IIa and IIx (the only style where the capillary itself, not just mitochondria/colour, is honestly rendered as thicker for IIa / thinner for IIx). Correct diagonal framing verified by pixel sample and corner crops; transverse+longitudinal striation confirmed on both fibres by magnified crops. 10-label SVG built; anchors for z_disc, sarcolemma and several plain-body points needed iterative refinement via colour-channel scans (nucleus-blue and Z-disc-grey were easy to confuse) before landing correctly, verified by final pixel sampling against the raw render.

used as final (gemini-3-pro-image). Attempt 1 failed framing -- both fibres showed a complete closed end-cap disc inside the canvas with visible paper margin on every side, caught by zooming the exit corners (the corner-pixel test alone would have passed it, since all 4 corners were correctly paper-toned regardless of the cap defect). Attempt 2, prompted to scale the bundle larger/closer and explicitly forbidding a paper-surrounded end-cap, came back correct: both fibres now run straight off the top-right and bottom-left corners, confirmed by magnified crops. Striation (perpendicular ink divider crossing the lengthwise hatching) and IIa/IIx colour+density differentiation both confirmed. 10-label SVG built with black-on-paper text override; every anchor pixel-sampled against the raw attempt-2 render.

used as final (gemini-3-pro-image), first API attempt. Two playful sausage-bodied cousin characters -- one mid-leap with a small round 'energy reserve' buddy shape (gestures at IIa's extra fatigue resistance without being literal), one mid-sprint and bigger (IIx, pure speed) -- holding hands/fist-bumping so they read as a duo. No starburst. The raw render DID come back with a thin rounded-rect border and a margin around the pair (a FAIL against the no-border/bleed-off-all-edges rule) -- fixed per the skill's documented lesson by measuring the border precisely (ring at pixel rows/cols ~45-51 and ~972-978 of 1024, with rounded corners reaching to local pixel 59 within each 60px corner) and cropping to (60,60)-(964,964) before re-tracing through coloring.py's own to_bitmap/trace_paths -- no second API call. Verified the corner crop fully removed the rounded-corner remnant (a first crop to (52,52)-(972,972) still left a faint corner arc, caught by zooming each corner individually, not just eyeballing the full image). Final SVG (34 paths, 26.6 KB) bleeds off the left, top and right edges and reads as one connected duo, not two separate drawings.
